novelty_flags.label: thm:colored-completeness / novelty_justification.strict_delta
novelty_flags.one_line: The prose says TCF sharpens de Aguas et al.'s sufficient criterion, but no statement proves Proposition 4 is a special case of TCF or exhibits a named strict-separation family.

soundness_flags.label: def:tcf-procedure and thm:colored-completeness
soundness_flags.one_line: TCF has signature TCF(G,A,Y) but its construction starts from Pobs, while the completeness iff has free Pobs only on the right; specify whether TCF is a universal graph decision procedure or a Pobs-indexed procedure and quantify compatible observed laws accordingly.

soundness_flags.label: thm:tcf-termination
soundness_flags.one_line: A 'finite real closed field presentation' is not a defined mathematical object; state a finite polynomial formula over the real closed field R, its variables, and the corresponding quantifier-elimination decision problem.

soundness_flags.label: prop:positive-subclass
soundness_flags.one_line: The proposition claims preservation of published FATE and NATE definitions, but the core defines only the natural query and tau; define FATE or remove that assertion.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PMLR landing record, abstract and bibliographic record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The proceedings paper introduces lm-SCMs/lm-graphs, FATE and NATE, and recovery criteria; the exact conclusion wording was corroborated only in arXiv:2506.15441v1 because the proceedings PDF text was inaccessible.
Algorithm 1 returns a formula or NA, and Theorem 5 states it always terminates and that any returned expression is correct; completeness is stated only for the no-label do-calculus special case.
For maximal-regular labels whose control variables are observed roots, Theorem 1 gives an iff reduction to every context DAG and Algorithm 1/Corollary 2 are sound and complete.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv manuscript used only as corroboration; journal primary text was inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Lemma 30 proves two simultaneously fixable vertices commute for graph and kernel; Theorem 31 extends invariance to valid sequences fixing the same set under the nested Markov model.
The paper develops a more general missing-data identification algorithm, requiring partial-order set removal and selected/latent subproblems, while describing a remaining general identification gap.
The article reduces discrete causal questions to polynomial programs and computes sharp ranges, including point identification, for declared assumptions and observed evidence.

The paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient graphical condition and algorithm for joint interventions in recursive semi-Markovian models, returning an expression or a hedge witnessing nonidentifiability.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make TCF's contract explicit: either define a symbolic universal graph procedure and quantify every compatible Pobs in the completeness theorem, or add Pobs to the input and state a pointwise fiber decision theorem; give the exact finite polynomial constraint system used at terminal states.

Add a comparator theorem proving that every de Aguas Proposition 4 instance is accepted by TCF with the same functional, plus a named lm-graph family where Proposition 4 fails while TCF succeeds; pair it with the existing Mokhtarian root-control reduction.

State an explicit termination bound in terms of vertex count, label/context count, trace length, polynomial-variable count, and quantifier-elimination input size, then retain the no-polynomial-time disclaimer.
Define the FATE functional alongside NATE or delete the unsupported FATE-preservation sentence from prop:positive-subclass.

recommended_next_step: Revise the TCF/fiber semantics and add an explicit de Aguas subsumption-and-strict-separation theorem before advancing the completeness kernel to Stage 0.
